elements.contents: ... that Mohamed Aw-Ali Abdi (pictured) campaigned in Birmingham, England, while running to become the vice president of Somaliland?

elements.contents: ... that most of the contributors to the Emancipation Pictorial, a Chinese women's magazine, were men?

elements.title: Elin Falk (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Elin Falk caused a national controversy in 1913 with her proposals for reforming gymnastics in Swedish schools?

elements.title: a new waltz (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the discovery of a new waltz attributed to Chopin was announced in October 2024?

elements.title: Adou Thiero (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that college basketball player Adou Thiero plays for the same head coach for whom his father played?

elements.title: Bejeweled (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that match-three video games such as Candy Crush Saga are often considered to be Bejeweled clones?

elements.title: Hikari Kodama (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Hikari Kodama disguised herself with wigs during public performances because she went to a high school with strict rules?

elements.title: three witnesses are typically needed (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that although three witnesses are typically needed in linguistic reconstruction, only two are necessary if borrowing and innovation can be ruled out?

elements.title: Mo Tzu-yi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that after seeing Taiwanese actor Mo Tzu-yi's work, a director sought to inquire about him at a film market, only to find Mo standing right behind him?
